article_title: Refining Statewide School Accountability Systems: Lessons from Innovative State Approaches under ESSA
citation: Mitch Herz, Mel Wylen. (2025). Refining Statewide School Accountability Systems: Lessons From Innovative State Approaches Under ESSA. White paper.
title: Ohio's Early Literacy Indicator within the SQSS Accountability Indicator
description: Ohio's accountability system includes an early literacy indicator tracking how well schools support K-3 students in developing reading skills, situated within the School Quality and Student Success indicator. Per the paper, "The Early Literacy Indicator tracks improvement in three areas: kindergarten readiness, grade 1 and grade 2 literacy improvement, and grade 3 reading proficiency." The accountability component formalizes commitment by tracking proficiency on the grade 3 ELA test, promotion to grade 4, and improvement among students previously off track, and is embedded in a broader ecosystem including the science of reading framework, dyslexia screening law, and mandated teacher PD.
requirements: Alignment with existing literacy screening requirements and accompanying supports such as targeted PD and state guidance
Centralized data systems and infrastructure for data integration
constraints: With multiple state-approved vendors, some districts struggled to align local tools with state reporting expectations; differences in cut scores and timing added confusion
target_learning_goals: early literacy and reading proficiency by the end of grade 3
examples: Ohio officials designed the indicator with districts and educators, aligning it with dyslexia screening and state-approved literacy curricula PD
key_sources: Mitch Herz, Mel Wylen. (2025). Refining Statewide School Accountability Systems: Lessons From Innovative State Approaches Under ESSA. White paper. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED677595

article_title: Measuring What Matters Most: Choice-Based Assessments for the Digital Age
citation: Daniel L. Schwartz and Dylan Arena. (2013). Measuring What Matters Most: Choice-Based Assessments for the Digital Age. The MIT Press. http://www.macfound.org
title: Ohno! Has Talent choicelet assessment for critical thinking
description: Ohno! Has Talent is a choicelet, defined as a short and engaging game that students want to complete and that requires some learning while logging students' choices relevant to that learning. In the game, students mix primary light colors to make contestants' preferred color beams across three rounds of increasing challenge, using an experiment room for safe trial and a faux shopping catalog of subtractive and additive color charts. Students must use critical thinking to decide which charts to believe, and the game logs their choices. Children play it in ten to twenty minutes.
requirements: A digital environment that logs students' choices in log files generated by the game
constraints: The authors describe the choicelet example as only promissory pending further research
target_learning_goals: Critical thinking as the process of deciding what to believe, and learning additive color mixing
examples: A student correctly mixed orange for contestant Otter by choosing two red lights and one green light in the final round
key_sources: Daniel L. Schwartz and Dylan Arena. (2013). Measuring What Matters Most: Choice-Based Assessments for the Digital Age. The MIT Press. http://www.macfound.org

article_title: Biting off More than They Can Chew? The Impact of Pedagogical Application of Corpus on Vocabulary Ability of Intermediate-Level ESL Learners in Mainland China: A Quasi-Experimental Study
citation: Jing Shi. (2017). Biting off More Than They Can Chew? The Impact of Pedagogical Application of Corpus on Vocabulary Ability of Intermediate-Level ESL Learners in Mainland China: A Quasi-Experimental Study. English Language Teaching, 10(9). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v10n9p232
title: Observe-Hypothesize-Experiment (OHE) data-driven learning cycle for corpus-based lexical teaching
description: The article implements corpus-based lexical instruction as a discovery process in which learners work with instructor-edited language data. Target lexical items are displayed in KWIC format, and learners "observe the language data, hypothesize the lexical use, report their hypothesis to the whole class, and finally find out the correct ways of using the target words." The article grounds this in a learning-by-doing principle and in the contextualized approach to L2 lexical teaching, positioning it as problem-based learning requiring collaboration.
requirements: Instructors edit and select the language data learners are exposed to
Teacher training on the corpus-based search engine is provided to students
Adequate instruction and teacher facilitation accompany the corpus work
constraints: Direct classroom use of corpora has given rise to many difficulties, per the literature the article cites
target_learning_goals: lexical awareness and contextualized word use
examples: Group A learners observed KWIC-displayed target items, hypothesized lexical use, reported hypotheses to the class, and verified correct usage over one semester.
key_sources: Jing Shi. (2017). Biting off More Than They Can Chew? The Impact of Pedagogical Application of Corpus on Vocabulary Ability of Intermediate-Level ESL Learners in Mainland China: A Quasi-Experimental Study. English Language Teaching, 10(9). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v10n9p232

article_title: Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX-based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia-a perspective.
citation: Ge Sheng-nan, Li Bing, Mu Bing-yan, Wan Li-sheng. (2026). Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX–based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia—a perspective. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1880936
title: OHL-Mini-CEX conceptual model expands Mini-CEX with three organizational health literacy assessment domains
description: The article proposes the "OHL-Mini-CEX" conceptual model, which "expands the conventional assessment scale by systematically embedding the universal precautions of OHL". It introduces three core assessment domains: teach-back evaluation, de-jargonization capacity, and empowering guidance, elevating communicative competence to an observable educational indicator in pediatric pneumonia case-based learning.
requirements: Communicative competence must be embedded as observable and measurable educational indicators within residency assessment
constraints: The proposed function remains conceptual and requires future empirical validation regarding its educational and organisational effects
target_learning_goals: communicative competence addressing health literacy barriers
key_sources: Ge Sheng-nan, Li Bing, Mu Bing-yan, Wan Li-sheng. (2026). Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX–based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia—a perspective. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1880936

article_title: Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX-based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia-a perspective.
citation: Ge Sheng-nan, Li Bing, Mu Bing-yan, Wan Li-sheng. (2026). Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX–based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia—a perspective. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1880936
title: Closed-loop pathway from micro-level OHL training to macro-level health equity outcomes
description: The article conceptualizes a theoretical closed-loop pathway with four stages: "educational encounters grounded in equity-conflict scenarios"; OHL-oriented Mini-CEX assessments with formative feedback; systematic aggregation of assessment findings to inform organizational learning and quality improvement; and potential long-term contributions to health equity. It is intended to depict a theoretical pathway rather than a confirmed causal sequence.
requirements: Institutionalization and scaling of OHL-infused assessment across an organization
constraints: The causal relationships proposed within this framework remain hypothetical and should be interpreted as testable propositions rather than established effects

article_title: Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX-based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia-a perspective.
citation: Ge Sheng-nan, Li Bing, Mu Bing-yan, Wan Li-sheng. (2026). Enhancing organizational health literacy through pediatric clinical training: Mini-CEX–based formative assessment in case-based learning for pediatric pneumonia—a perspective. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1880936
title: Integrate health literacy communication competencies as core performance indicators in residency education rather than desirable personal attributes
description: The article argues that communicative competencies such as systematic identification of low health literacy, standardized teach-back, and empathetic plain-language communication "should cease to be treated as desirable personal attributes" and instead be integrated as core performance indicators within residency education and mandatory steps within organizational care protocols, so OHL becomes an institutionalized organizational capability.
requirements: Embedding communication skills as integral components of institutional workflow
constraints: Upstream administrative simplifications remain isolated, superficial fixes if clinical conversation skills are not embedded
examples: The OHL-Mini-CEX operationalizes this by making teach-back verification a core assessment domain
key_sources: Ge Sheng-nan, Li Bing, Mu Bing-yan, Wan Li-sheng. (2026). article_title: Improving membranous urethral length measurements on prostate MRI: a comparison of online training methods.
citation: Goedegebuure E.P., Boellaard T.N., van Dijk-de Haan M.C., et al. (2026). Improving membranous urethral length measurements on prostate MRI: a comparison of online training methods. European Radiology 36(8):6419-6427. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00330-026-12468-w
title: Web-based training platform combining OHIF DICOM viewer with electronic case report forms for MUL measurement training
description: A dedicated web-based training platform "which combines the Open Health Imaging Foundation (OHIF) DICOM viewing platform with electronic case report forms," customized for this study. It supported three steps: baseline testing on 20 cases without feedback, group-specific training protocols (written instructions, self-study with feedback forms, or expert-led sessions), and post-training retesting. Group B participants received feedback via "annotated key images, common pitfalls, and practical tips, as well as reference measurements embedded in the DICOM series."
requirements: T2-weighted MRI sequences in three planes with adequate visualization of the membranous urethra.
Reference measurements based on average values from two faculty members.
constraints: The platform was customized specifically for this study by two of the authors.
target_learning_goals: accurate MUL measurement on prostate MRI
examples: The platform hosted 20 test cases and 40 training cases randomly selected from a previous research database, all acquired on 3-Tesla MR systems.
key_sources: Goedegebuure E.P., Boellaard T.N., van Dijk-de Haan M.C., et al. (2026). Improving membranous urethral length measurements on prostate MRI: a comparison of online training methods. European Radiology 36(8):6419-6427. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00330-026-12468-w

article_title: Educational videos as a teaching approach to enhance dental students' practical skills in preclinical courses.
citation: Dervisbegovic Selma, Laky Markus, Tur Dino, Grundnig Julia, Rausch-Fan Xiaohui, Moritz Andreas, Holzinger Anita. (2025). Educational videos as a teaching approach to enhance dental students’ practical skills in preclinical courses. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07807-2
title: Two short high-quality instructional videos on the Bass technique and interdental brushing
description: Two professionally filmed instructional videos demonstrated oral hygiene instruction: the first covered the Bass technique and bristle position for all tooth surfaces, and the second demonstrated measuring interdental spaces with a calibrated probe and interdental brushing, with "a duration of approximately three minutes". Both included audio descriptions of key points. Quality was defined by four criteria: content accuracy, clear instructional structure with step-by-step demonstrations and voice-over, professional production standards, and appropriate length to maintain attention.
requirements: Content reviewed and approved by a panel of medical and dental educators to confirm each questionnaire item was adequately addressed in the video
constraints: Controlled video access did not allow viewing at students’ own pace, which the authors note may not reflect real-life learning behaviour
target_learning_goals: interdental space assessment and correct interdental brush selection and use
examples: Videos were filmed on a Canon 5D Mark III in 1080p, edited in Adobe Premiere, and shown once or four times over four consecutive weeks before a practical test
key_sources: Dervisbegovic Selma, Laky Markus, Tur Dino, Grundnig Julia, Rausch-Fan Xiaohui, Moritz Andreas, Holzinger Anita. (2025). Educational videos as a teaching approach to enhance dental students’ practical skills in preclinical courses. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07807-2

article_title: Perceived mental health skills and competence among occupational health physicians.
citation: Majuri M, Malin M, Antila A, Luukkonen R, Palosaari M, Reijula K. (2024). Perceived mental health skills and competence among occupational health physicians. Occupational Medicine (Oxford, England). https://doi.org/10.1093/occmed/kqae080
title: Develop the OH specialist physician curriculum with new educational approaches and courses targeting workplace-level proactive mental health competences
description: Because respondents acknowledged weaker competence in community-based proactive workplace-level actions, the authors recommend curriculum development: "Occupational health services must target services towards work–life transformation, which requires new educational approaches and courses for the occupational health physician curriculum." None of the current fragmented courses handle proactive collaboration between workplaces and OH services or community-level actions, so mental health education should gain a dedicated place in the curriculum and EPAs.
requirements: Education should be coupled with curriculum and expert coaching, and trainees learn by executing workplace activities to achieve competence
constraints: The authors state further research is needed to assess whether OH specialist training and new courses influence physicians' skills, and how a competence-based curriculum influences mental health competences
target_learners: trainee physicians in OH specialist physician training
target_learning_goals: workplace-level proactive mental health competences such as assessing psychosocial and cognitive risks and promoting workplace resources
examples: The survey found workplace-level items such as promoting psychological, social and cognitive resources of the workplace rated lowest (trainer 3.17 [1.05], trainee 2.93 [0.97])
key_sources: Majuri M, Malin M, Antila A, Luukkonen R, Palosaari M, Reijula K. (2024). Perceived mental health skills and competence among occupational health physicians. Occupational Medicine (Oxford, England). https://doi.org/10.1093/occmed/kqae080

article_title: The evaluation of e-learning resources as an adjunct to otolaryngology teaching: a pilot study.
citation: Chin Ronald Yoon-Kong, Tjahjono Richard, Rutledge Michael John Raymond, Lambert Tim, Deboever Nathaniel. (2019). The evaluation of e-learning resources as an adjunct to otolaryngology teaching: a pilot study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1618-7
title: Interactive OHNS e-learning video resources with layered information, interactive questions and end-of-video quizzes
description: A set of interactive e-learning teaching resources designed by the authors to supplement the University of Sydney OHNS curriculum, covering thyroid, rhinological, otological, oral and head & neck clinical examinations in videos lasting approximately 26 minutes. "Layered information and interactive questions were placed at intervals throughout the video resources, where students can decide to interact as they see fit," and a quiz at the end of each video supports self-assessment and knowledge retention. Access was provided through a unique link and login details.
requirements: Requires internet-based delivery with unique links and login details for student access
constraints: Usage of the resources was not logged due to system limitations, so the study could not quantify how often students used them
target_learning_goals: OHNS clinical examination skills and knowledge (thyroid, rhinological, otological, oral, head & neck examinations)
examples: Videos of OHNS clinical examinations lasting approximately 26 minutes, with layered information, interactive questions at intervals, and an end-of-video quiz for self-assessment
key_sources: Chin Ronald Yoon-Kong, Tjahjono Richard, Rutledge Michael John Raymond, Lambert Tim, Deboever Nathaniel. (2019). The evaluation of e-learning resources as an adjunct to otolaryngology teaching: a pilot study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1618-7

article_title: A 5-day intensive curriculum for interns utilizing simulation and active-learning techniques: addressing domains important across internal medicine practice.
citation: Dversdal Renee K., Gold Jeffrey A., Richards Matthew H., Chiovaro Joseph C., Iossi Katherine A., Mansoor André M., Hunter Alan J., Desai Sima S. (2018). A 5-day intensive curriculum for interns utilizing simulation and active-learning techniques: addressing domains important across internal medicine practice. BMC Research Notes. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13104-018-4011-4
title: 5-day OHSU internal medicine intern 'Intensive Week' simulation curriculum
description: A sequential 5-day curriculum held at the OHSU Simulation Center, with 2 days as one cohort and 3 days rotating through six half-day stations in groups of 5–6. Content targets five needs: managing urgent calls, difficult conversations, EHR proficiency, standardized procedural training, and point-of-care ultrasound. It uses "high-fidelity case-based simulations, procedural simulation with task trainers, communication simulations with standardized patients, and electronic health record (EHR) simulated exercises".
requirements: All 'Intensive Week' clinical obligations covered by upper level residents so interns participate for 5 consecutive days
A minimum of six faculty members over 5 days, approximately 14 faculty per year for a total of 312 hours
constraints: Requires substantial departmental commitment for faculty time and protected time for interns
Significant time commitment in training faculty to participate, which decreases with return faculty
target_learning_goals: Procedural skills (ABG, PIV, CVC, lumbar puncture, paracentesis, thoracentesis)
examples: In 2014, 33 interns and in 2015, 32 interns completed the curriculum with 100% pre-survey participation and 96% overall post-survey completion
key_sources: Dversdal Renee K., Gold Jeffrey A., Richards Matthew H., Chiovaro Joseph C., Iossi Katherine A., Mansoor André M., Hunter Alan J., Desai Sima S. (2018). A 5-day intensive curriculum for interns utilizing simulation and active-learning techniques: addressing domains important across internal medicine practice. BMC Research Notes. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13104-018-4011-4
